title: The Generative AI stack
subtitle: From language models to the chips and energy behind them. Explore the layers that turn a model into an assistant—and the physical infrastructure that makes it possible.

sections.title: Models & assistants
sections.label: The software layer
sections.intro: Explore how language models are developed through pre-training and post-training, and distinguish a base model from the assistant or agent built around it. Use this section to connect model capabilities with the application layer.
sections.question: What does an assistant add around a language model? Consider instructions, tools, memory and the interface.

resources.title: Large language models
resources.description: The LLM lecture selected for Module 1. Use it as a starting point for exploring the model layer.

sections.title: Chips & data centres
sections.label: The physical layer
sections.intro: Follow the stack from software to physical infrastructure. This section brings together semiconductor supply chains and the data centres that house computing hardware.
sections.question: Where can a bottleneck in the physical stack constrain the development or deployment of AI?

resources.title: Chips and the semiconductor industry
resources.description: The chips lecture selected for Module 1. Connect the semiconductor industry to the infrastructure behind AI.

resources.title: The AI supply chain & infrastructure
resources.description: Suggested reading: the AI supply chain and the different types of infrastructure that support it.

sections.title: Energy & AI
sections.label: Powering the stack
sections.intro: Examine the relationship between AI and electricity: the energy used to train and run models, the needs of data centres, and the wider energy system. The IEA report provides the main reading for this section.
sections.question: How would you distinguish the energy required for training from the energy required to serve users over time?

resources.title: Energy and AI
resources.description: Full report. Suggested starting points: executive summary (p. 13), model life cycle (p. 39) and Energy for AI (p. 49).

sections.title: DeepSeek & energy
sections.label: Case study
sections.intro: Bring the layers together through the Module 1 case study. Use the report’s discussion of model efficiency and inference-time scaling to examine the relationship between technical improvements and energy demand.
sections.question: Does a more efficient model necessarily mean lower total electricity demand? What evidence would you need to answer that question?

resources.title: Model efficiency and inference
resources.meta: IEA · Energy and AI · Start at p. 43
resources.description: Suggested case-study reading on model architecture, inference-time scaling and the energy implications of reasoning models, including DeepSeek-R1.
